zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Ghāshiya
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هَلْ أتاكَ حَدِيثُ الغاشِيَةِ﴾ ("has the report of the Overwhelming come to you?"): it was said that al-Ghāshiya is the Resurrection, because it overwhelms (taghshā) creation; and it was said: al-Ghāshiya is the Fire, because it covers the faces of the unbelievers.

zajjaj:2-2.t: ﴿وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ خاشِعَةٌ﴾: ”خاشِعَةٌ“ is the khabar (predicate) of ”وُجُوهٌ“, and the meaning of ”خاشِعَةٌ“ is "abased".

zajjaj:3-3.t:
And the meaning of ﴿عامِلَةٌ ناصِبَةٌ﴾ ("toiling, weary"): it was said that they toil and weary themselves in this world for what does not bring them near to Allah the Exalted; and it was said that they are the monks and those resembling them; and it was said ﴿عامِلَةٌ ناصِبَةٌ﴾ in the Fire, so He described their suffering of the punishment.
And His saying, in the description of the people of Paradise: ﴿لا تَسْمَعُ فِيها لاغِيَةً﴾ [al-Ghāshiya: 11] ("you will not hear therein idle talk"). It was also read ”لا يَسْمَعُ فِيها لاغِيَةً“, and it was read ”لا تُسْمَعُ فِيها لاغِيَةٌ“ (passive, "no idle talk will be heard therein"), that is: nothing sinful will be heard therein. It is also possible that [it means] ”لا تَسْمَعُ فِيها كَلِمَةً تُلْغى“ ("you will not hear therein a word that is lughā"), i.e. that is dropped [as worthless]: the people of Paradise speak only wisdom and praise of Allah for the everlasting bliss He has provided them.

zajjaj:4-4.t: ﴿تَصْلى نارًا حامِيَةً﴾ ("they will roast in a blazing Fire"); it is also read ”تُصْلى“ (passive: "they will be made to roast").

zajjaj:5-5.t: And His saying: ﴿تُسْقى مِن عَيْنٍ آنِيَةٍ﴾: that is, extreme in intensity of heat, like His saying: ﴿يَطُوفُونَ بَيْنَها وبَيْنَ حَمِيمٍ آنٍ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 44] ("they will circulate between it and scalding water, intensely hot").

zajjaj:6-6.t: ﴿لَيْسَ لَهم طَعامٌ إلا مِن ضَرِيعٍ﴾: He means for the people of the Fire. ”اَلضَّرِيعُ“ is al-shibriq, a kind of thorn: when it is fresh it is ”شِبْرِقٌ“, and when it dries it is ”اَلضَّرِيعُ“. The unbelievers of Quraysh said: "Our camels grow fat on ḍarīʿ!" So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿لا يُسْمِنُ ولا يُغْنِي مِن جُوعٍ﴾ [al-Ghāshiya: 7] ("which neither fattens nor avails against hunger"). And the meaning of ﴿هَلْ أتاكَ﴾ [al-Ghāshiya: 1] is: "Was this not outside your knowledge and the knowledge of your people?" And likewise the narratives which He related to the Prophet ﷺ; Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿ما كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُها أنْتَ ولا قَوْمُكَ مِن قَبْلِ هَذا﴾ [Hūd: 49] ("neither you nor your people knew them before this").

zajjaj:14-14.t: And His saying: ﴿وَأكْوابٌ مَوْضُوعَةٌ﴾: ”اَلْأكْوابُ“ are vessels resembling ewers, without handles.

zajjaj:15-15.t: ﴿وَنَمارِقُ مَصْفُوفَةٌ﴾ ("and cushions lined up"): its singular is ”نُمْرُقَةٌ“.

zajjaj:16-16.t: ﴿وَزَرابِيُّ مَبْثُوثَةٌ﴾: ”اَلزَّرابِيُّ“ are carpets; its singular is ”زَرْبِيَّةٌ“.

zajjaj:17-17.t: And His saying: ﴿أفَلا يَنْظُرُونَ إلى الإبِلِ كَيْفَ خُلِقَتْ﴾ ("do they not look at the camels, how they were created?"): Allah drew their attention to something mighty among His creation which He has made submissive, so that a small child leads it, breeds it and makes it rise; a heavy load is put on it while it is kneeling, and it rises with its heavy load, and that is not found in any other beast of burden. So He showed them something mighty among His creation in order to guide them thereby to His oneness (tawḥīd).

zajjaj:18-18.t: ﴿وَإلى السَّماءِ كَيْفَ رُفِعَتْ﴾: He means: without pillars.

zajjaj:19-19.t:
﴿وَإلى الجِبالِ كَيْفَ نُصِبَتْ﴾: they were set up as firmly anchored [mountains] that do not move away.
﴿وَإلى الأرْضِ كَيْفَ سُطِحَتْ﴾ [al-Ghāshiya: 20]: that is, it was spread out and laid flat.

zajjaj:21-21.t: ﴿فَذَكِّرْ إنَّما أنْتَ مُذَكِّرٌ﴾ ("so remind; you are only a reminder"): this was before the Prophet ﷺ was commanded to fight.

zajjaj:22-22.t: ﴿لَسْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِمُصَيْطِرٍ﴾: that is, [you are not] one given authority [over them].

zajjaj:23-23.t: ﴿إلا مَن تَوَلّى وكَفَرَ﴾ ﴿فَيُعَذِّبُهُ اللَّهُ العَذابَ الأكْبَرَ﴾ [al-Ghāshiya: 24] ("except whoever turns away and disbelieves, Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment"): that is, the punishment of Hell.

zajjaj:25-25.t: ﴿إنَّ إلَيْنا إيابَهُمْ﴾ ("to Us is their return"). It was also read ”إيّابَهُمْ“; [the word is read] with both the light and the doubled [yāʾ]. The meaning of ”إيابَهُمْ“ is "their return"; and the meaning of ”إيّابَهُمْ“ is as a maṣdar (verbal noun) of ”أيَّبَ، إيّابًا“, on the pattern ”فَيْعَلَ“, ”فِيْعالًا“, from ”آبَ، يَؤُوبُ“ ("to return"). The original form is ”إيْوابًا“; then the yāʾ was assimilated into the wāw, and the wāw changed into yāʾ because it was preceded by a sukūn. [Translator's note: so in the source; in the usual statement of this rule the wāw becomes yāʾ and the first yāʾ is then assimilated into it.]
